results.summary: Mean (max-min)/max rises with saturation: 0.2735 at 1.0, 0.3957 at 1.5, 0.4945 at 2.0. At saturation 0 the frame is monochrome: mean cross-channel gap is only 0.01 code values (rounding noise from the matrix coefficients, not colour). No crash found anywhere in the 2.0-2.5 range including the schema max of 2.5: _saturation_chain now splits saturation above SAT_MAX_PER_PASS into several composed colorchannelmixer passes (s ** (1/N) each, exactly equivalent by the matrix's own idempotent-luma-projection algebra) specifically to stay inside ffmpeg's [-2, 2] coefficient range, so the whole schema range now renders without error.

results.summary: Local variance (variance of the on-minus-off difference image, minus a 3x3 box blur of that difference; isolates the added noise from scene content) is 0.10 at strength 10 and 2.12 at strength 90, rising with strength. Two independent ffmpeg invocations of the SAME grain config, at the same clip and timecode, produced byte-identical frames for every config tested here (run-to-run spread 0 in all cases). That contradicts this audit brief's own assumption that grain is random per ffmpeg run: for a single still frame the noise plate is grabbed from frame 0 of a freshly started lavfi noise source every time, so a still-frame render of a given config is fully reproducible; a real video render over many frames would show a different noise realisation per output frame instead.
results.direction: claim: strength up raises local variance; measured 0.10 -> 2.12

results.summary: The noise plate itself is r==g==b at every pixel (True: confirmed by direct array comparison, not inferred), so the source noise is exactly monochrome as the code comment claims. Once blended onto the real, coloured, textured frame via overlay blend, the visible result is NOT perfectly monochrome: cross-channel correlation of the on-minus-off residual is r-g=0.7322, r-b=0.6008, g-b=0.6393. This is expected, not a bug: overlay blend is a function of each channel's own base value, so the same luma-only perturbation lands as a different absolute delta per channel wherever the base image itself has colour.
